result.title: Tucker Bottleneck Attention for Multi-Dimensional Sequence Modeling
result.summary: The quadratic cost of self-attention limits scalability to long sequences from multidimensional data. We introduce Tucker bottleneck attention (TuBA), which exploits low-rank tensor structure for efficient global token mixing. TuBA projects hidden tensors into compact Tucker cores, performs multi-head self-attention and linear projections on the cores, and writes updates back to the ambient space, enabling subquadratic computation. Its autoregressive extension combines bidirectional interactions within cores with causal attention across cores. On video prediction and global weather forecasting, TuBA achieves favorable accuracy-efficiency trade-offs over standard and efficient attention and task-specific models. Compared to standard self-attention, TuBA reduces error and computation by up to 24.7% and 66.6% for video prediction and 37.1% and 85.1% for autoregressive weather forecasting, with speedups up to 4.27 times. Low-rank Tucker cores and multi-frame generation also outperform full-rank attention and frame-by-frame generation, respectively.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文提出 Tucker bottleneck attention（TuBA），利用低秩张量结构把隐状态投影到紧致 Tucker 核心上做多头注意力与线性变换，再写回原始空间，实现次二次复杂度，并在视频预测与天气预测上取得精度—效率折衷。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「核心空间注意力 + 写回」的低秩瓶颈思路，可能与 LVR 中压缩视觉/推理状态、控制 latent token 规模与动态计算成本的问题相关，属于表示压缩层面的潜在启发，尚需核查是否保留任务必要的视觉细节与实体关系。
